items.entity: rectangular design domain (span between clamped sides × height)
items.description: Sec. 4.1 says the 'structural dimensions' are in Fig. 8(a). The text only says the beam is rectangular 'with its width greater than its length'. That gives no aspect ratio and does not say which dimension is the horizontal span between the clamped sides. Absolute sizes are also only in the figure; they matter if Lmin or a filter radius is a physical length.
readings: span:height = 1:2 (taller than wide, if 'length' means the horizontal span)

items.description: Sec. 4.1 says 'A horizontally downward force is applied at the top center'. 'Horizontally' contradicts 'downward'.
readings: horizontal (±x) along the top edge at mid-span (the two signs give mirror-image layouts)

items.description: Sec. 4.1 only says the force is 'applied at the top center'. It does not say whether this is one nodal force or a traction spread over a short patch, or how wide the patch is.
readings: single concentrated nodal force at the top mid-span node
uniform traction over a short centred patch (about 2–5% of the span)
force split over the 2–3 top nodes nearest mid-span

items.description: The text gives no force value; boundary conditions are referred to Fig. 8(a). Secs. 4.2.1 and 4.3.1 ('Their information is the same with double clamper beam case') imply the low-fidelity runs use a different force magnitude from the high-fidelity model, but neither value is stated.
Secs. 4.1 and 4.1.1 never mention non-design regions. The Fig. 8(a) caption refers to 'the design space', which may or may not be the whole rectangle.
readings: small solid non-design pad under the top-center load
thin solid non-design strips along the clamped left/right edges

items.description: Sec. 4.1.1 generates '160 different solutions by varying the V0 from 0.25 to 0.50'. It does not say how V0 is sampled within that range.
readings: evenly spaced with step 0.25/160 = 0.0015625 (one endpoint excluded)

items.entity: V0 of the 15 representative designs in Fig. 8(b)
items.description: Sec. 4.1.1 says Fig. 8(b) shows five designs per Lmin 'arranged in increasing volume fraction order'. Their V0 values appear only in the figure.

items.entity: volume measure V(μ1, μ2, ρ) and the equivalent single-material volfrac
items.description: Eq. (33) requires V(μ1, μ2, ρ) ≤ V0, but V is never defined (Secs. 2.1, 3.2, 4.1.1). It could be the solid area of the cross cells with effective bar widths μ1ρ and μ2ρ (Eq. 32), or just the lattice-filled fraction ρ. So it is unclear what volfrac to give a single-material solver.
readings: V = domain average of the cross-cell solid fraction μ1ρ + μ2ρ − μ1μ2ρ²; single-material volfrac = V0
V = domain average of ρ (lattice-filled area), so the actual solid fraction is below V0
V = domain average of (μ1 + μ2)ρ (bar overlap neglected)

items.description: Sec. 4.1.1 calls Lmin a 'minimum feature size', but Eq. (33) uses it only as a lower bound on the relative bar widths μ1 and μ2; the effective widths μ1ρ and μ2ρ in Eq. (32) can still reach zero. No reference length is given, and a single-material solver has no direct equivalent. Yet the text says Lmin changes the topology (larger Lmin gives more large voids).
readings: treat it as a pure bound on relative bar width with no single-material counterpart: ignore it (one run per V0, 160 designs instead of 480)
minimum member size = Lmin × domain height, enforced through the filter radius or a length-scale control
minimum member size = Lmin in the physical units of Fig. 8(a)

items.entity: upper bound L_max on μ1, μ2
items.description: Eq. (33) includes an upper bound L_max on the bar widths, but no value is given.

items.entity: density bounds ρ_min, ρ_max and void (Ersatz) stiffness
items.description: Eq. (33) bounds ρ by ρ_min ≤ ρ ≤ ρ_max without values. No void or minimum stiffness is given for the low-fidelity finite-element model.

items.entity: homogenized stiffness surrogate C^H(μ1, μ2) of the cross cell
items.description: Eq. (4) does not report the polynomial orders q_max and r_max, the coefficients α_ij, the (μ1, μ2) sampling grid, or the unit-cell mesh used for homogenization; the curves appear only in Fig. 2(b). This is the stiffness–density law that produced the Fig. 8 designs.
readings: re-homogenize the cross cell (E = 1, ν = 0.3) on a fine grid and fit with q_max = r_max = 4
same, with q_max = r_max = 6 or higher
use an analytical rank-2 laminate / cross-bar stiffness approximation instead

items.entity: solid–void interpolation / penalization for a single-material solver
items.description: Sec. 3.2 says the interpolation scheme is 'adapted accordingly' for each case. Eq. (31) only scales the bar widths by ρ inside C^H. No SIMP- or RAMP-type penalty is given for an equivalent single-material solid–void model.
readings: no penalization (p = 1), allowing grey lattice-like regions

items.description: The paper never says whether the model is plane stress or plane strain; Sec. 3.2 gives only E = 1 and ν = 0.3.
No out-of-plane thickness is given for the 2D model (Secs. 3.2, 4.1).
readings: the thickness shown in Fig. 8(a), if any

items.description: The paper does not give the number of macro elements N_m (coarse mesh N_c), or the element type and shape, for the low-fidelity optimization. The COMSOL free-triangle mesh (Secs. 2.2.2, 4) is used only for the high-fidelity evaluation.
readings: about 30 square Q4 elements over the height (e.g. 60×30 for a 2:1 domain)
about 50 square Q4 elements over the height (e.g. 100×50)
about 100 square Q4 elements over the height (e.g. 200×100)

items.description: Secs. 3.2 and 4.1.1 give no filter type, filter radius or projection for the low-fidelity optimization.
readings: density filter, r_min ≈ 3 elements (or tied to Lmin) with Heaviside projection

items.entity: optimizer, starting design and stopping criteria
items.description: The paper gives no optimizer (OC or MMA), move limit, iteration limit, convergence tolerance, or starting values of ρ, μ1, μ2 and θ. It also does not say whether the three Lmin runs per V0 start fresh or from a previous solution. The problem is non-convex, so these choices affect the layouts.
readings: MMA, uniform start ρ = V0, up to 200–300 iterations
OC, move limit 0.2, uniform start ρ = V0, stop when the max change is below 0.01
each Lmin run warm-started from the previous V0/Lmin solution instead of a uniform start

items.description: Eq. (33) leaves obj(·) generic. Sec. 3.2 says 'stiffness optimization' and Sec. 4.2.1 says 'stiffness maximization', but the stiffness measure for this beam in Sec. 4.1.2 is maximum displacement.
readings: compliance FᵀU (same as load-point displacement for a single point load)

locator: Sec. 4.1.1, the double-clamped beam, low-fidelity stiffness designs (Fig. 8)
